```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

#Question 1

```{r}
bdays = sample(1:365, 25, replace = TRUE)

length(unique(bdays)) < 25
```

```{r}
bday = function(n) {
  if (!is.numeric(n)) {
    stop("n must be numerical")
  } else if (n<2) {
    stop("group has at least 2 ppl")
  }
  
  bdays = sample (1:365, n, replace = TRUE)
  
  any(duplicated(bdays))
}

bday(10)
bday(50)
```

```{r}
bday_function_df =
  expand.grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared = map_lgl(group_size, bday)
  )

prob_df =
  bday_function_df |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarise(prob_shared = mean(shared))
```


```{r}
prob_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = prob_shared)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of shared birthday",
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Probability of shared birthday"
  )
```
The probability of a shared birthday rises steadily as group size increases. The smaller the group size is, the lower probability there is of having a shared birthday. It reaches 50% probability at around a group size of 23 and increases to 96% probability at a group size of 48 and plateaus afterwards.


#Question 2

```{r}
data_df = "data/data/"

participant_df =
  tibble(
    files = list.files(data_df),
    path = str_c(data_df, files)
  ) |>
  mutate(data = map(path, read_csv)) |>
  unnest(cols = data)
```

```{r}
tidy_df =
  participant_df |>
  mutate(
    files = str_replace(files, ".csv", ""),
    arm = str_sub(files, 1,3)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "outcome",
    names_prefix = "week_"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week))|>
  select(arm, subj = files,week, outcome)
```
This is the tidy dataset with `r nrow(tidy_df)` rows and `r ncol(tidy_df)` columns. The variables of the columns are `r names(tidy_df)`. Depicting the arm (control vs experimental) a participant is in, the participant subject ID, week, and outcome data.

## Spaghetti plot
```{r}
tidy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome, group = subj, color = arm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~arm) +
  labs(
    title = "Outcome of each participant over time",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome",
    color = "Arm"
  )
```
Particpants in the control arm begin with outcome measures between 0 and 2.5. Participants in the experimental arm begin with outcome measures around the same level between -1 and 3.75. Over time, participants in the control arm remain relatively steady with outcome measures that remain fairly constant. By Week 8, outcome measure remain between around 0 and 2.5. However, for the experimental arm, over time outcome measures increase steadily for all participants. By Week 8, outcome measure rise between 2.5 and 7.5.

#Question 3

```{r}
t_test_df = function(mu, n = 30, sigma = 5) {
  
  test_data_df = tibble(
    x = rnorm(n, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  )
  test_data_df |>
    pull(x) |>
    t.test(mu = 0) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    select(estimate, p.value)
}
```

```{r}
model_df =
  expand_grid(
    mu = 0:6,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    results_df = map(mu, t_test_df)
  ) |>
  unnest(results_df) |>
  mutate(reject = p.value < 0.05)
```
